  GOAL nutrition_carbohydrate:
    name "Carbohydrate 90-130 g per day, mostly low-GI whole foods, consistent meal timing, pair carbs with protein and fibre"

  GOAL nutrition_fats_hydration:
    name "Unsaturated fats (olive oil, nuts, oily fish 2x per week), limit saturated fat, water 2-2.5 L per day, limit alcohol"

    name "Intermittent or time-restricted fasting not prescribed. Extended fasting windows conflict with metformin hypoglycaemia risk, fed morning cardio, post-session snacks, and glucose checks. Use 3 regular meals with consistent timing and planned snacks instead. Revisit only with prescriber approval"
  GOAL morning_cardio_fed:
    name "Morning cardio on Tuesday and Thursday is always fed, never fasted. Pre-session breakfast 30-60 minutes before: 200 g plain Greek yogurt (about 20 g protein) with 30 g rolled oats (about 20 g carbohydrate) and 80 g berries (about 10 g carbohydrate, total 30 g carbohydrate), or 2 boiled eggs with 1 slice wholegrain toast and a small piece of fruit. Check glucose before starting; stop and eat if glucose below 5 mmol/L or symptoms of hypoglycaemia appear"
  GOAL post_workout_snacks:
    name "After strength sessions, eat within 60 minutes a snack of about 20-30 g protein with 15-30 g low-GI carbohydrate: 150 g plain Greek yogurt with 80 g berries; 2 boiled eggs with 1 slice wholegrain toast; 100 g cottage cheese with 1 apple; 30 g hummus with wholegrain crackers and cucumber; 1 small tin of sardines on wholegrain toast. Check glucose after sessions; if below 5 mmol/L, take fast-acting glucose first, then eat"
  GOAL weekly_planned_meal:
    name "One planned flexible meal per week, on Saturday, not on a training day. Limit to one meal (about 600-700 kcal), not a full day of eating. Build it around protein and vegetables, include some carbohydrate, and keep to a normal portion size. Absorb the extra calories within the weekly energy budget by eating slightly lighter on the other days. Avoid alcohol with the meal and avoid sugary drinks. Check glucose before the meal and 2 hours after. If glucose is above 10 mmol/L at 2 hours, skip the planned meal next week and review with the prescriber. The meal should not replace glucose checks, medication timing, or any safety actions"
  GOAL diabetic_safety:
    name "Glucose check before and after sessions if meter available; carry fast-acting glucose; do not train fasted; no training if glucose below 5 mmol/L or above 14 mmol/L with ketones; never stop metformin or change medication without prescriber advice; foot checks daily; report symptoms of hypoglycaemia promptly"
  GOAL monitoring:
    name "Weekly weight and waist, fortnightly fasting glucose log, repeat HbA1c at week 12"

    name "Unsaturated fats (olive oil, nuts, oily fish 2x per week), limit saturated fat, water 2-2.5 L per day, limit alcohol"

    name "Intermittent or time-restricted fasting not prescribed. Extended fasting windows conflict with metformin hypoglycaemia risk, fed morning cardio, post-session snacks, and glucose checks. Use 3 regular meals with consistent timing and planned snacks instead. Revisit only with prescriber approval"
  GOAL morning_cardio_fed:
    name "Morning cardio on Tuesday and Thursday is always fed, never fasted. Pre-session breakfast 30-60 minutes before: 200 g plain Greek yogurt (about 20 g protein) with 30 g rolled oats (about 20 g carbohydrate) and 80 g berries (about 10 g carbohydrate, total 30 g carbohydrate), or 2 boiled eggs with 1 slice wholegrain toast and a small piece of fruit. Check glucose before starting; stop and eat if glucose below 5 mmol/L or symptoms of hypoglycaemia appear"

    name "After strength sessions, eat within 60 minutes a snack of about 20-30 g protein with 15-30 g low-GI carbohydrate: 150 g plain Greek yogurt with 80 g berries; 2 boiled eggs with 1 slice wholegrain toast; 100 g cottage cheese with 1 apple; 30 g hummus with wholegrain crackers and cucumber; 1 small tin of sardines on wholegrain toast. Check glucose after sessions; if below 5 mmol/L, take fast-acting glucose first, then eat"

    name "One planned flexible meal per week, on Saturday, not on a training day. Limit to one meal (about 600-700 kcal), not a full day of eating. Build it around protein and vegetables, include some carbohydrate, and keep to a normal portion size. Absorb the extra calories within the weekly energy budget by eating slightly lighter on the other days. Avoid alcohol with the meal and avoid sugary drinks. Check glucose before the meal and 2 hours after. If glucose is above 10 mmol/L at 2 hours, skip the planned meal next week and review with the prescriber. The meal should not replace glucose checks, medication timing, or any safety actions"

plan.name: Fat Loss and Glycaemic Control, 12 Weeks

goals.name: Reduce body fat while lowering HbA1c from 7.2 toward 6.5 or below
Improve insulin sensitivity through resistance training and post-meal walking
Energy intake 1500-1700 kcal per day, approx 500 kcal deficit, set against baseline intake
Protein 1.2-1.6 g per kg bodyweight per day, spread across 3 meals, 25-35 g per meal
Carbohydrate 90-130 g per day, mostly low-GI whole foods, consistent meal timing, pair carbs with protein and fibre
Fibre 25-35 g per day from vegetables, legumes, oats, seeds, and low-GI fruit
Unsaturated fats (olive oil, nuts, oily fish 2x per week), limit saturated fat, water 2-2.5 L per day, limit alcohol

Intermittent or time-restricted fasting not prescribed. Extended fasting windows conflict with metformin hypoglycaemia risk, fed morning cardio, post-session snacks, and glucose checks. Use 3 regular meals with consistent timing and planned snacks instead. Revisit only with prescriber approval

Morning cardio on Tuesday and Thursday is always fed, never fasted. Pre-session breakfast 30-60 minutes before: 200 g plain Greek yogurt (about 20 g protein) with 30 g rolled oats (about 20 g carbohydrate) and 80 g berries (about 10 g carbohydrate, total 30 g carbohydrate), or 2 boiled eggs with 1 slice wholegrain toast and a small piece of fruit. Check glucose before starting; stop and eat if glucose below 5 mmol/L or symptoms of hypoglycaemia appear

After strength sessions, eat within 60 minutes a snack of about 20-30 g protein with 15-30 g low-GI carbohydrate: 150 g plain Greek yogurt with 80 g berries; 2 boiled eggs with 1 slice wholegrain toast; 100 g cottage cheese with 1 apple; 30 g hummus with wholegrain crackers and cucumber; 1 small tin of sardines on wholegrain toast. Check glucose after sessions; if below 5 mmol/L, take fast-acting glucose first, then eat

One planned flexible meal per week, on Saturday, not on a training day. Limit to one meal (about 600-700 kcal), not a full day of eating. Build it around protein and vegetables, include some carbohydrate, and keep to a normal portion size. Absorb the extra calories within the weekly energy budget by eating slightly lighter on the other days. Avoid alcohol with the meal and avoid sugary drinks. Check glucose before the meal and 2 hours after. If glucose is above 10 mmol/L at 2 hours, skip the planned meal next week and review with the prescriber. The meal should not replace glucose checks, medication timing, or any safety actions

Glucose check before and after sessions if meter available; carry fast-acting glucose; do not train fasted; no training if glucose below 5 mmol/L or above 14 mmol/L with ketones; never stop metformin or change medication without prescriber advice; foot checks daily; report symptoms of hypoglycaemia promptly
Weekly weight and waist, fortnightly fasting glucose log, repeat HbA1c at week 12
